project_title: Effects of anti-H. pylori triple therapy and a probiotic complex on intestinal microbiota in duodenal ulcer
project_description: Case-control baseline comparison of the fecal (stool) microbiota of 40 Helicobacter pylori-positive active duodenal ulcer patients versus 20 healthy check controls in China, profiled by 16S rDNA V4 amplicon sequencing for bacteria and internal transcribed spacer (ITS) sequencing for fungi.
citation: Wu et al. 2019, Sci Rep, PMID 31492912
notes: Sample type: FECAL/stool. Pre-treatment (baseline) comparison, 40 H. pylori-positive active duodenal ulcer patients vs 20 healthy check controls; ulcer site = duodenum. Significance was nominal (two-tailed p<0.05); no FDR/multiple-testing correction reported. H. pylori status of the healthy controls is not stated in the paper. Verbatim source statement: 'There were a total of 55 differential bacteria at the genus level, 54 of which were less in the DU group than those in the HC group, except the Natronomonas genus that increased in the DU group.' The 54 depleted genera are NOT individually named anywhere in the paper (no table/figure lists them), so no rows were created for them. No exact p-value or effect size is reported for this genus. CAUTION: Natronomonas is an extreme-halophilic archaeal genus and this call is plausibly a Greengenes annotation artifact; transcribed verbatim from the paper, not independently endorsed.

project_title: Helicobacter pylori infection alters gastric microbiota structure and biological functions in patients with gastric ulcer or duodenal ulcer
project_description: Case-control shotgun metagenomic sequencing of GASTRIC MUCOSAL BIOPSY specimens from 4 Helicobacter pylori-positive gastric ulcer patients and 4 H. pylori-negative healthy individuals in China (a third arm of 4 duodenal ulcer patients was sampled at the duodenal mucosa and is not used here).
citation: Jin et al. 2024, World J Gastroenterol, PMID 38983956
notes: Sample type: GASTRIC MUCOSAL BIOPSY - NOT fecal/stool. Ulcer site = stomach (gastric ulcer). Verbatim source statement: 'Sixteen species, including Rhizobium oryzihabitans, Klebsiella oxytoca, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Rhizobium hidalgonenses, and Agrobacterium fabrum, were enriched in the gastric mucosal microbiota of healthy individuals (group C)' - i.e. depleted in gastric ulcer patients. Only 5 of the 16 species are named in the text; the remaining 11 are not named and were not recorded. Very small cohort: n=4 gastric ulcer vs n=4 healthy. All cases were H. pylori-positive and all controls were H. pylori-negative by design, so the ulcer effect is fully confounded with H. pylori infection status. LEfSe threshold was LDA>2; no per-taxon LDA score or p-value is reported and no FDR correction is reported.
